newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends up, Central Bk intervenes.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends up, Central Bk intervenes.

text.p: * Volume heavy at $236.7 million from $159.5 million
The Philippine peso closed higher on Friday at 26.365 from the previous close of 26.37 after the Central Bank flooded the market with about $91 million at 26.37, traders said.
The day's average, however, was unchanged at 26.367.
Offshore funds tested the Central Bank's resolve to defend the peso at 26.37 as the peso continued to fall prey to the outflow of arbitrage money in recent days, dealers said.
The same offshore funds returned later after the Central Bank showed its strong hand at 26.37 pesos.
"With the Central Bank being tested at 26.37 and holding firm, we'll see inflows next week," a foreign bank dealer said.
"Funds believe the peso will be stable again," he continued, adding that the peso could trade from 26.355/26.37.
Giving support to the peso too is the expected consolidation in interest rates following the news that inflation in March rose to 4.8 percent from 4.4 in February.
The benchmark 91-day T-bill remained at a single-digit level for the third consecutive week on Monday at 9.498 percent.
